note: Re-judged 2026-11-10 (independent judge, authored neither the row, the tests nor 202ee384e9). Stale because the cited producer internal/component/ike/dataplane/xfrm_linux.go::xfrmStateFromParams moved after the previous stamp: the stamp recorded during 202ee384e9 predates the committed unit, whose doc comment now names DontEncapDSCP and OSeqMayWrap (XFRM_SA_XFLAG_DONT_ENCAP_DSCP and XFRM_SA_XFLAG_OSEQ_MAY_WRAP in XFRMA_SA_EXTRA_FLAGS) beside ESN, AFUnspec, NoPMTUDisc and ICMP. The pre-stamp unit is not recoverable for a byte diff, so the whole committed function was re-read instead of trusting the comment-only account. Statements: mode and SPI 0 refusals, the mixed-family tunnel refusal, the replay window, OSeqMayWrap=false (present before 202ee384e9), the masked state selector, AFUnspec, the inbound-only ICMP flag, planStateAlgos (dataplane.go, unchanged in 202ee384e9: ESP non-AEAD sets Crypt and Auth), xfrmEncName, xfrmAuthName, the UDP encap template, xfrmNoPMTUDisc and xfrmDontEncapDSCP. Section 4.2, read in rfc/full/rfc4301.txt: "Note: A compliant implementation MUST NOT allow instantiation of an ESP SA that employs both NULL encryption and no integrity algorithm." On every ESP SA without AEAD the builder calls xfrmAuthName(p.AuthAlgo), and xfrmAuthNames holds only sha256, sha384, sha512 and sha1, so an empty or "none" integrity algorithm returns ErrNotSupported and no state; null is not in xfrmAEADNames, so it cannot take the AEAD branch. Nothing 202ee384e9 added touches the encryption or integrity fields, and each addition is a flag or a further refusal. The tagged units are unchanged: TestRFC4301ESPNullEncryptionWithIntegrityIsInstantiated asserts the exact null cipher and hmac(sha256) transform, TestRFC4301ESPNullEncryptionWithoutIntegrityIsRefused asserts refusal and a nil state for "" and "none"; the VPP and OSPF config tags cover the other instantiation paths as before. Enforced stands.
